themeData.name: Golden Age of Rail
themeData.tagline: Dining car recipes from the great American railroads
themeData.description: From the Harvey House restaurants along the Santa Fe to the elegant Pullman dining cars, these recipes defined travel luxury in the early 20th century.
themeData.coverImagePrompt: Elegant vintage train dining car with white tablecloths and art deco details, golden hour light through windows, watercolor illustration

recipes.title: Harvey House Corned Beef Hash
recipes.description: The famous breakfast served to weary travelers at Harvey House restaurants along the Santa Fe Railroad.
recipes.story: Fred Harvey's restaurants transformed railroad dining from a rushed necessity into an experience. This hash was served on china plates by the famous Harvey Girls, giving travelers their first taste of Western hospitality.
instructions: Combine corned beef, potatoes, and onion in a large bowl. Add cream, Worcestershire, salt, and pepper. Mix well.
Melt butter in a large cast-iron skillet over medium heat.
Spread hash mixture evenly in the skillet. Press down firmly with a spatula.
Cook without stirring until bottom is golden and crispy, about 8-10 minutes.
Flip sections of hash and press down again. Cook another 8-10 minutes until crispy.
Make 4 wells in the hash. Crack an egg into each well.
Cover and cook until eggs are set to your liking, about 5 minutes.
Garnish with parsley and serve immediately.

recipes.title: Harvey House Tossed Green Salad
recipes.description: The refreshing salad that greeted travelers with crisp greens and tangy house dressing.
recipes.story: Fred Harvey insisted on the freshest ingredients, remarkable for restaurants in remote desert towns. This simple salad was a revelation to travelers who expected only dried goods on the frontier.
instructions: Combine lettuces in a large salad bowl.
Arrange tomatoes, cucumber, and radishes on top.
Whisk together olive oil, vinegar, mustard, garlic, sugar, salt, and pepper in a small bowl.
Drizzle dressing over salad just before serving. Toss gently at the table.

recipes.title: Harvey House Chili con Carne
recipes.description: The Southwest specialty that introduced Eastern travelers to bold frontier flavors.
recipes.story: For Easterners riding the Santa Fe into New Mexico, Harvey House chili was often their first encounter with Southwestern cuisine. Many requested the recipe, only to find it impossible to replicate without the proper dried chiles.
instructions: Brown ground beef in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Drain excess fat.
Add onions and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add garlic and cook 1 minute.
Stir in chili powder, cumin, oregano, and cayenne. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add tomatoes, tomato paste, broth, and salt. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer uncovered for 45 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add beans if using and cook 15 minutes more.
Serve with crackers or cornbread.

recipes.title: Great Northern Railway Pot Roast
recipes.description: Tender beef braised to perfection, the hearty centerpiece of Sunday dinner service.
recipes.story: Crossing the northern plains, the Great Northern Railway offered pot roast as Sunday dinner. The beef braised slowly as the train climbed through the Rockies, filling the dining car with an irresistible aroma.
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F (165°C).
Season roast generously with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a large Dutch oven over high heat. Sear roast on all sides until deeply browned, about 10 minutes total. Remove and set aside.
Add onions, carrots, and celery to pot. Cook until beginning to brown, about 5 minutes.
Stir in tomato paste and garlic. Cook 1 minute.
Add broth, wine, bay leaves, and thyme. Bring to a simmer.
Return roast to pot. Cover and transfer to oven.
Braise 2 hours. Add potatoes and continue cooking until beef is fork-tender, about 1 hour more.
Let rest 15 minutes before slicing. Serve with vegetables and pan juices.

recipes.title: Pennsylvania Railroad Salmon Croquettes
recipes.description: Crispy fried salmon cakes with a creamy center, served with dill sauce.
recipes.story: The Pennsylvania Railroad's Broadway Limited was famous for its cuisine. These salmon croquettes were a Friday special, crispy on the outside with a savory, herb-flecked center.
instructions: Combine salmon, 1/2 cup breadcrumbs, egg, onion, celery, lemon juice, dill, salt, and cayenne.
Shape into 8 oval croquettes.
Roll croquettes in remaining breadcrumbs to coat.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Fry croquettes until golden brown, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Drain on paper towels.
Mix sour cream, mayonnaise, and dill for sauce.
Serve croquettes with dill sauce.

recipes.title: Harvey House Lemon Meringue Pie
recipes.description: Tart lemon filling topped with billowing meringue—the pie that made Harvey House famous.
recipes.story: The gleaming pie cases at Harvey House displayed these lemon meringue beauties like precious gems. The contrast of tangy lemon against sweet, fluffy meringue was perfection on a plate.
instructions: Whisk sugar, cornstarch, and salt in a saucepan. Gradually whisk in water.
Cook over medium heat, whisking constantly, until thickened and bubbling.
Whisk egg yolks in a bowl. Slowly whisk in 1/2 cup hot mixture to temper.
Return to saucepan. Cook, whisking, 2 minutes more.
Remove from heat. Stir in butter, lemon zest, and lemon juice.
Pour into pie crust.
Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Beat egg whites and cream of tartar until soft peaks form. Gradually add sugar, beating to stiff peaks.
Spread meringue over hot filling, sealing to edges.
Bake until meringue is golden, about 15 minutes.
Cool completely before slicing.

recipes.title: Pullman Car Chicken à la King
recipes.description: Creamy chicken in a rich sherry sauce, served in the elegant dining cars of the Pullman Company.
recipes.story: In the golden age of rail travel, Pullman dining cars were rolling restaurants of extraordinary elegance. Chicken à la King, with its creamy sauce and touch of sherry, epitomized the refined service travelers expected.

ingredients.name: toast points or puff pastry shells
ingredients.text: toast points or puff pastry shells

instructions: Melt butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add mushrooms and bell pepper; cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Sprinkle flour over vegetables and stir to coat. Cook 2 minutes.
Gradually whisk in broth and cream. Bring to a simmer, stirring until thickened.
Whisk egg yolks in a small bowl. Slowly whisk in 1/2 cup of hot sauce to temper.
Return tempered yolks to pot, stirring constantly.
Add chicken, pimientos, sherry, salt, and pepper. Cook until heated through, about 5 minutes.
Serve immediately over toast points or in puff pastry shells.

recipes.title: Santa Fe Railroad Cinnamon Rolls
recipes.description: Soft, gooey cinnamon rolls that perfumed the dining cars each morning.
recipes.story: The aroma of fresh cinnamon rolls announced breakfast service in dining cars across America. Bakers worked through the night in swaying kitchens to ensure these were ready by sunrise.
instructions: Dissolve yeast in warm milk (110°F). Let stand 5 minutes until foamy.
Add sugar, melted butter, egg, and salt to yeast mixture. Gradually add flour to form a soft dough.
Knead until smooth and elastic, about 5 minutes. Place in a greased bowl, cover, and let rise 1 hour.
Punch down dough. Roll into a 16x12-inch rectangle.
Spread softened butter over dough. Sprinkle with brown sugar and cinnamon.
Roll up tightly from the long side. Cut into 12 rolls.
Place in a greased 9x13 pan. Cover and let rise 30 minutes.
Bake at 350°F (175°C) for 25-30 minutes until golden.
Beat cream cheese, powdered sugar, and vanilla until smooth. Spread over warm rolls.

recipes.title: Pullman Waldorf Salad
recipes.description: The elegant salad of apples, celery, and walnuts in creamy dressing, a staple of first-class dining.
recipes.story: The Waldorf Salad, created at New York's Waldorf-Astoria Hotel, became a symbol of refined dining aboard Pullman cars. It traveled well and offered a refreshing counterpoint to heavier main courses.
instructions: Toss diced apples with lemon juice to prevent browning.
Whisk together mayonnaise, sour cream, remaining lemon juice, honey, and salt.
Combine apples, celery, walnuts, and grapes in a large bowl.
Add dressing and toss gently to coat.
Serve on butter lettuce leaves.

recipes.title: Harvey House Coconut Layer Cake
recipes.description: A towering white cake covered in clouds of coconut frosting—the celebrated dessert of Harvey House.
recipes.story: This magnificent cake was displayed under glass domes at Harvey House restaurants. Travelers often ordered a slice to go, wrapped in wax paper for the journey ahead.
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease and flour three 9-inch round pans.
Beat butter and sugar until light and fluffy. Add eggs one at a time, then vanilla.
Whisk flour, baking powder, and salt. Add to butter mixture alternately with buttermilk.
Divide batter among pans. Bake 25-30 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool in pans 10 minutes, then turn out onto racks to cool completely.
For frosting: Beat butter and cream cheese until smooth. Add powdered sugar and vanilla; beat until fluffy.
Frost between layers and all over cake. Press coconut onto top and sides.

recipes.title: Southern Pacific Bread Pudding
recipes.description: Rich, custardy bread pudding with whiskey sauce—a railcar dessert legend.
recipes.story: The Sunset Limited's bread pudding was legendary. Baked fresh each evening, it arrived at tables drizzled with warm bourbon sauce—the perfect finale to a transcontinental journey.
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C). Butter a 9x13 inch baking dish.
Place bread cubes in the dish. Scatter raisins over top.
Whisk together milk, cream, eggs, sugar, vanilla, and cinnamon.
Pour custard over bread. Let soak 30 minutes, pressing bread down occasionally.
Bake until set and golden, about 50-60 minutes.
For sauce: Melt butter in a saucepan. Add brown sugar and cream. Simmer 5 minutes.
Remove from heat and stir in bourbon.
Serve warm bread pudding with whiskey sauce.

recipes.title: The Classic Railroad Club Sandwich
recipes.description: The triple-decker sandwich invented for railroad dining, stacked with turkey, bacon, and all the fixings.
recipes.story: The club sandwich was designed for one-handed eating aboard rocking trains. Its triple-decker construction became an American icon, though few remember its railcar origins.
instructions: Toast all bread slices until golden.
Spread mayonnaise on one side of each slice.
Layer first slice (mayo up) with turkey, lettuce, and tomato. Season.
Add second slice (mayo side up), then bacon.
Top with third slice (mayo side down).
Secure with toothpicks. Cut diagonally into quarters.
Serve with chips or fries.
